My own image folder

Choose a folder of PNG / JPG / GIF / WebP images on your computer. Sub-folders become groups. Progress is remembered per folder name, so you can come back later and pick the same folder again.

Sharing the work: send someone this page's link. They open their image folder, tag, hit Export JSON, and send you the images plus figure-tags.json. To give them your tag list first, export your own JSON and have them Import it before starting — only the tag palette is taken from a file that has no matching images. Tag palette (key toggles)

New tags get the next free hotkey and stay in the palette for every later image.
Enter done + next · Shift+Enter/← prev · → next (no mark)
] next not-done · n new tag · Del clear · click image to zoom

Manage tags

Renaming updates every image that has the tag. Deleting removes it from every image. Hotkeys follow palette order.

Keys

Tag hotkeys, in palette order: 1–6 q w e r t, then 7–0 a s d f g, then z x c v b, y u i o p, h j k l.
Enter mark this image done and go to the next one.
Shift+Enter or ← previous image · → next image without marking it.
] jump to the next image that is not done yet.
n focus the new-tag box; Enter there creates the tag and adds it to this image; Esc leaves the box.
Delete clear all tags on this image. Click the image to toggle full-size zoom.

Saving

Everything is saved in this browser immediately. Link save file… also writes figure-tags.json to disk after every change (Chrome, Brave, Edge), so the tags survive clearing browser data. Export JSON / Import JSON do the same by hand; Export CSV gives a file,tags spreadsheet.

Sharing with a coworker

Send them this page's link. They choose their own image folder, tag, and send you the images plus their exported figure-tags.json. If you want them to use your tag names, send them your exported JSON to Import first — a file with no matching images only contributes its tag palette.
